\[
\rho = x \cos\theta + y \sin\theta,
\qquad
H(\theta, \rho) \ge 10
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\theta, \rho\): The normal angle and distance of a line
- \(H\): The accumulator of votes

The progressive probabilistic Hough transform of Matas and coworkers votes with one edge pixel at a time, in random order, in the same accumulator of lines as the standard transform. When a line reaches the vote threshold, the filter follows that line from the pixel that voted last, in both directions, and jumps over gaps up to the largest gap. A segment is kept when it spans the shortest length in x or in y. Its pixels are then removed from the edges and their votes from the accumulator. Pixels on a found segment never get their turn to vote, which saves time. The order is random, so this filter fixes the seed and gives the same result each time.
